text:
alex: heads-up — ACME prod hitting steady tail latency + intermittent 429s after a warmup period. started ~10:12 PDT, kept ramping then tokens started failing. attaching short logs.

priya: which dedicated pool / pool-id?

alex: pool eu-west-1 / rdw-cedar-3, reserved capacity. customer says they requested 2x80G equivalent slots but our placement returned MIG partitions (smaller slices). saw throughput drop after autoscaler tried to add capacity.

support-bot: New ticket #12345 created (escalation).

james: can you paste one of the failing request ids and a sample error body? also sharing the curl helps.

alex: posted sample response snippet:

```
HTTP/1.1 429 Too Many Requests
Content-Type: application/json
{
  "error": "quota_exceeded",
  "reason": "slot_throttle",
  "request_id": "req_01F..."
}
```

alex: logs show token latency spiking then 429s across many requests, not a single client.

monica: checking infra metrics — I see short SM_util spikes on the host and L3 cache thrashing during the same window. Looks like a noisy-sibling burst on the node.

eng-sre: pinging @oncall — autoscaler created new instances but the mig bindings failed briefly; driver logs show repeated `mig create` timeouts.

oncall: investigating — kernel shows `nvidia-mig: partition binding timeout` and some cgroup evictions when power cap temporarily increased. Could be a host-level power-management bounce from another tenant's workload.

priya: that matches reported behavior: warmup runs fine, then when another tenant started a heavy kernel (non-mig full GPU job) the MIG slices experienced contention. This isn't classic scheduler throttling, it's cross-slice interference due to shared L3 / memory bandwidth.

james: do we have request-level evidence it correlates with the other tenant? any host id?

monica: host id is host-eu-12. I pulled audit logs — another customer launched a cuda batch job on the same host for ~45s starting 10:12:41. SM and PCIe counters spike there.

alex: customer wants root cause + mitigation. They reported no unexpected billing charge, just degraded QoS.

eng-sre: short-term mitigations applied: removed the instance from the active rotation, rebalanced affected slots to a different host class, and temporarily bumped their burst capacity so requests route to isolated nodes. Cleared prefix/KV cache to reduce backpressure.

priya: recommended medium-term actions: prefer_isolated_nodes flag for dedicated pools (we already have this in config but wasn't set for this fleet), and add a pre-bind validation step in the autoscaler to verify MIG slice availability before marking slot ready.

monica: long-term: add a probe after node provision that runs `nvidia-smi -q -d MIG` and `nvidia-smi topo -m` plus a micro-benchmark to detect L3/DRAM contention. If probe fails, reprovision a fresh host. Also export `mig_binding_failures` metric for alerting.

james: also suggest adding a soft-isolation policy where we avoid co-locating long-running non-MIG workloads with MIG partitions in the same host class.

priya: i'll open a PR to add the probe and an autoscaler gating check. will also add an alert: `mig_binding_failures > 0 for 2m` -> P2 and page oncall.

alex: customer accepted temporary move to isolated nodes and is OK waiting for the autoscaler fix. They asked for a short RCA summary.

eng-sre: RCA summary for ticket: transient noisy-neighbor interference on host-eu-12 — non-MIG full-GPU batch job caused L3/memory bandwidth contention leading to MIG slice performance degradation and slot-level throttles. Autoscaler created new slots but some bindings timed out — contributing to 429s. Mitigations: moved customer to isolated nodes, added backlog smoothing, will add autoscaler pre-bind checks and probe.

support-bot: ticket #12345 updated with RCA and mitigation steps. escalation tag cleared.

alex: thanks team — please follow up with customer tomorrow for verification. :thumbsup:

priya: noted, i'll include repro steps and a config snippet to enable preference for isolated nodes:

```
pool_config:
  prefer_isolated_nodes: true
  node_affinity: "no-shared"
  autoscaler:
    prebind_probe: true
```

monica: also tagging eng-runtime to consider adding a cheap micro-benchmark during warmup to catch interference early.

alex: closing thread after customer confirmation.
